send.description: A message to send the agent through the channel, once per crossing, as `rig agent send` would.

Action.description: Action is what one watch threshold does when crossed.

harness.description: claude-code, the default when left out. The harness decides the binary, how it is installed and launched, and which credentials it authenticates with.

prompt_file.description: The brief: a file on this host, relative to this file, sent once when the session is created; later changes reach the agent as diffs.

workdir.description: Where the agent works in the guest: /work when left out.

model.description: The model, as the harness names it; the guest's default when left out.

timeout.description: Kill one run after this long (6h when left out) and resume it: the outer backstop for a run that never reaches a turn boundary, not a mission limit. A healthy run it cuts loses a few minutes to reconciliation; idle_timeout is the one that fires only on a run that has stopped working.

idle_timeout.description: Kill one run after this long with no tool call in its event log, and resume it with a note saying so. A run that is visibly working is never interrupted. Off when left out; 20m is a reasonable value.

memory_max.description: MemoryMax= on the agent's unit, in systemd's syntax: 80% when left out, of the guest's memory, so a runaway child is killed before the guest hits a global OOM and takes the agent with it.

until_done.description: Treat a clean exit as a turn boundary, not a result: resume until the agent runs `rig done`. Off when left out, as the honest default for an unattended process.

budgets.description: Hard limits. Crossing one stops the agent the way `rig agent stop` does, at once, with a BUDGET marker saying which fired and at what value; the session is kept, so raising the budget and running `rig agent start` resumes it where it stopped.

watch.description: Soft thresholds. Each crossing and clearing is a `rig agent watch` event and a line in `rig agent status --full`; on: may add a message. Nothing here stops the agent.

oneOf.description: Agent is guest.agent in its long form.

Agent.description: Agent is guest.agent in its long form.

hours.description: Wall-clock hours since `rig agent start`, restarts included.

tokens.description: Tokens consumed over the session, in and out, cache reads and writes included, summed from the harness's own event log.

usage.description: A subscription window's utilization, where the credential has one (an OAuth login; an API key has none); read from the provider on the host.

restarts.description: Restarts since `rig agent start`, turn boundaries included; beyond this the unit is not restarted again. Distinct from the burst limit that stops a flapping unit within the hour.

Budgets.description: Budgets is guest.agent.budgets: what an unattended agent may not run past.

kind.description: `gpu`: an NVIDIA card (the guest needs rig.nixosModules.nvidia). `pci`: any PCI function, such as a USB controller. `usb`: one USB device, by id.

pci.description: The PCI address, from lspci -D, for gpu and pci. It must be alone in its IOMMU group.

id.description: For usb, vendor:product from lsusb. For gpu and pci, vendor:device from lspci -nn: what must be at the address, since a BIOS change can renumber the bus. Required for pci.

return.description: How the host takes a gpu or pci device back after rig stop. Without it, the device stays on vfio-pci, which suits hardware the host never uses.

Device.description: Device is one host device a VM may be given.

image.description: An image alias already built (rig image build). Give this or flake.

flake.description: A flake to build the image from, as <name>-guest when missing: ./guest builds nixosConfigurations.guest, ./guest#daw builds .daw, and remote references (github:me/vms?dir=guest) work too.

cpus.description: A number of vCPUs, or a set of host CPUs to pin them to, one each ("4-7,12-15"): for a guest with deadlines, such as audio.

env_file.description: A file of KEY=VALUE credentials, injected to tmpfs in the guest at each start and never written to its disk. Keep it outside any repository.

devices.description: Which of host.devices this VM gets.

ports.description: Guest ports published on a host address, in Compose's syntax. Each one opens that port alone through the isolation ACL, through the network, and can be bound to an address other machines reach. For your own preview of something the guest serves, forwards is the default and this the exception.

forwards.description: Guest ports carried to this host's loopback over vsock, which is not IP: the isolation ACL that `rig verify` proves is untouched, the port exists on 127.0.0.1 of this host only, and a host process holds it (rig start leaves one, rig-forward-<vm>, that ends with the VM and is left again at the next start). The manifest form of `rig forward`; it works with network: none too, since no NIC is involved.

volumes.description: Named Incus volumes mounted in the guest. They outlive the VM, so data survives it being recreated; host directories are refused.

network.description: none: no network device at all. Left out, the VM gets the isolated NIC, which reaches the internet but not this host or the LAN.

input.description: host: lend this host's keyboard and mouse to the guest as events from start to stop, toggled with both Ctrl keys. The guest needs rig.nixosModules.desktop.

agent.description: The coding agent `rig agent` runs in this guest, and how: the harness name alone (claude-code, the default), or a block with the run's settings, which `rig agent start` reads as its defaults; a flag given to it wins, and is recorded until the file's settings next change.

proxy.description: The host's proxy (witmproxy), which this guest reaches over a second NIC that leads nowhere else. Its one job so far is credentials the guest never holds: see proxy.credentials. Set up once per host with `rig proxy setup`.

anyOf.description: Devices by a name of your choosing, which guest.devices refers to.

devices.description: Devices by a name of your choosing, which guest.devices refers to.

host_ip.description: The host address to publish on, such as its tailnet address to keep the port off the LAN. The LAN address when left out.

published.description: The host port, or a range a-b.

target.description: The guest port, or a range a-b the same size. Defaults to published.

oneOf.description: Port is one published port, in Compose's terms: Published is the host side, Target the guest side, each a port or an inclusive range "a-b".

Port.description: Port is one published port, in Compose's terms: Published is the host side, Target the guest side, each a port or an inclusive range "a-b".

credentials.description: Variables from env_file whose values the guest never sees, each with the endpoints the value may be sent to. The guest gets a stand-in; the proxy puts the real value into HTTPS requests to those endpoints, and nowhere else, wherever the stand-in occurs in a header or the URL. An endpoint is "[METHOD[,METHOD] ]host[/path]": the host alone is every request to it; a path covers itself and everything below it; *.host covers the host and its subdomains. A guest that leaks everything it has leaks a string that works only through this proxy, only there: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: [POST api.anthropic.com/v1/messages]

egress.description: What else the guest may reach through the proxy. Left out, nothing: the proxy dials the credentials' hosts and refuses the rest. internet: everything the isolated NIC may reach, with this host and the LAN still refused, judged on the address after resolution. For the tools under the agent, which inherit its HTTPS_PROXY: cargo, git, nix and npm reach their registries through the proxy or not at all.

Proxy.description: Proxy is guest.proxy: what the host's proxy does for this guest.

modules.description: Kernel modules to unload before the unbind and reload after the reset; the NVIDIA driver needs this.

reset.description: Reset the device before the host driver binds it. A card handed back from a guest may not initialise without it. rig start moves the device onto vfio-pci before the VM starts, so its stop leaves it there for the reset; both steps run under sudo.

alive.description: A glob under the device's sysfs directory that exists once the host driver has really brought it up: drm/card* for a card, usb* for a USB controller.

unit.description: A host systemd unit that uses the device, such as display-manager: stopped before a VM claims it, started after it comes back.

Return.description: Return is how the host takes a device back after rig stop.

max.description: The fraction of the window, above 0 and at most 1: 0.9 is 90%.

Usage.description: Usage is a subscription window and a fraction of it.

source.description: The volume's name; created in the VM's storage pool when missing.

target.description: Where the guest mounts it: an absolute path.

owner.description: uid:gid that owns the volume's root when it is created, such as 1000:100 for the desktop user. Root otherwise.

oneOf.description: Volume is one entry of guest.volumes: an Incus custom storage volume by name, and where the guest mounts it.

Volume.description: Volume is one entry of guest.volumes: an Incus custom storage volume by name, and where the guest mounts it.

idle_minutes.description: Minutes with no new commit on the branch checked out in the workdir.

unit_minutes.description: Minutes a transient unit the agent started (systemd-run: a dev server, a build) has been running.

units.description: A glob naming which transient units count, such as "mono-*". Every transient service but rig's own when left out.

usage.description: A subscription window's utilization, as under budgets, as a warning.

on.description: What a crossing does besides the event: by threshold (idle, unit, status, usage), a message to send the agent, so it is asked to account for itself. The event alone when left out.

Watch.description: Watch is guest.agent.watch: facts about the run rig observes without the harness's help, each with the point past which the operator wants to hear.

host.description: Devices on this host that a VM may be given. It repeats per project, so one file describes everything its VM needs.

guest.description: The VM, and what it is given.

title: rig.yaml
description: Manifest is a rig.yaml: what one VM is given.
